title: world.counters gpu reports the world engine's counted work for its newest completed submission, pass by pass in order, identically on both backends
binding: The positive leg boots a still offscreen world with one SDF view, waits for the engine to be ready (world.wait ready: its pipeline set installed and its first frame produced), and reads the gpu section of world.counters sixty completed ticks later and again after thirty more. The world node's line in each response carries its submission, and the second read's is greater: a later submission. The world node's nine pass lines appear in pass order. Upload's counts and the node's created buffers follow the device's residency policy (a device whose memory profile rings every table writes the one viewport word in place; one that stages records a copy, a transition and a header and run entry beside the word, over more buffers), which is why SdfWorldEngine.PassClasses makes upload per-backend-deterministic, so the canary names the upload line and the created-buffer count without pinning either, as puck counters does not hold the backends to them, and pins no machine's policy. Sky through views read skipped exactly because the cadence gate leaves the view's retained output standing for the still frame, so no image is transitioned; the work outside every pass is exact, and the node's created objects follow with no pipeline or shader module among them, because the shared SDF pipeline cache creates and counts those under gpu.sdf-pipelines, and with its four images, two descriptor pools and thirty-eight sets, which no residency policy changes, since the engine reserves every region's copy sets whatever policy the device selects. The pass pipelines count under their own source, gpu.pass-pipelines: two pipelines and two shader modules, the device's region copy and the one place pipeline the root's four place passes share. The root, main, places the world's one view through its four place passes, none of which shows anything, so each draws nothing and none dispatches: the chain stands for the world, and each pass line carries only its planned barriers. The exact lines hold on Vulkan and Direct3D 12 alike, which is the cross-backend proof. The discriminating leg reads world.counters gpu twice before the first tick, when no submission has completed, so neither read shows a pass line and the positive's exact lines turn red.
